Abstract: Here, the authors establish NaCdCo 2 F 7 as a spin-orbit-entangled J eff =½ pyrochlore antiferromagnet, in which strong geometric frustration and bond disorder drive unconventional spin freezing. item.title: [7] Magnetic-field-driven phase switching in the antiferromagnetic Mott insulator Ca3(Ru0.99Ti0.01)2O7
item.description:
Last authors: Bernhard Keimer, Alexander V. Boris

Authors: Ksenia S. Rabinovich, Tim Priessnitz, Nils Gross, et al.

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Magneto-transport and phase transitions in correlated ruthenates are highly relevant.

Tags: #magnetism #Mott #transport

Abstract: Isovalent 1% Ti substitution tunes the polar metal Ca 3 Ru 2 O 7 to the edge of its Mott transition. While electronic kinetic energy and strong electron-lattice coupling contribute to the system’s free-energy balance, its magnetic H - T phase diagram is remarkably simple, closely resembling that of a canonical anisotropic antiferromagnet, albeit with substantially renormalized critical fields. Along the easy axis, a first-order spin-flop transition near 6 Tesla reorients the Ru moments while the system remains insulating; a forced-ferromagnetic metal emerges above 10.5 Tesla field.

item.title: [9] Significant modulation of acoustoelectric current associated with charge density wave transitions
item.description:
Last authors: Shintaro Takada, Yasuhiro Niimi

Authors: Natsumi Nikaido, Takuya Kawada, Koji Fujiwara, et al.

Score 9/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Direct experimental study of CDW in NbSe2/TaSe2 relevant to quasi-1D and CDW interests.

Tags: #CDW #NbSe2 #transport #vanderWaals

Abstract: How collective electronic order responds to strain remains a central question in quantum materials. Here, the authors find that charge density wave (CDW) transitions in NbSe 3 and 2 H -TaSe 2 strongly modulate the acoustoelectric current driven by surface acoustic waves. A simple phenomenological model based on strain-dependent conductivity captures the essential behavior. The work demonstrates acoustoelectric transport as a sensitive probe of CDW physics and opens new avenues for strain-based control of electronic states in van der Waals materials.

item.title: [7] Ab initio quantum embedding description of magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene at even-integer fillings
item.description:
Last authors: Steven G. Louie, Lin Lin

Authors: Raehyun Kim, Woochang Kim, Kevin D. Stubbs, Steven G. Louie, Lin Lin

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: High-quality ab initio work on magic-angle graphene, relevant to moiré physics.

Tags: #graphene #moiré #DFT

Abstract: The correlated phase diagram of magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene (MATBG) is very sensitive to both material parameters and modeling choices. To limit the impact of these factors, here, the authors propose an embedding workflow for modeling MATBG and other moiré materials that incorporates automatic gauge fixing and is consistent with a b i n i t i o density functional theory. Using this workflow, the authors find that in MATBG, the Hartree-Fock ground state at ν = − 2 is a fragile semimetal with intervalley coherence.

item.title: [7] Visualizing vortex cluster dynamics in the weakly type-II superconductor CaSb2
item.description:
Last authors: Nabhanila Nandi, Mohamed Oudah

Authors: Yusuke Iguchi, Nabhanila Nandi, Mohamed Oudah

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Visualization of superconducting vortex dynamics, good condensed-matter experimental work.

Tags: #superconductivity #vortices

Abstract: Here, the authors use scanning SQUID microscopy to visualize magnetic dynamics within superconducting vortex clusters, revealing suppressed vortex motion in the interior and enhanced response at the boundaries. These spatially inhomogeneous dynamics, hidden from static magnetic imaging, provide a new way to probe the interactions that hold vortices together and distinguish between mechanisms of vortex clustering.
